bands.value: Band 7 (9-8 line); SV continuum-mode data covering 6-5 near 230 GHz

evidence.quote: Mira was observed by ALMA again in Band 7 on 21 July 2015 reaching the best resolution and sensitivity so far at these wavelengths.
The spectra cover four ranges, 342.1–344.0, 344.1–346.0, 354.2–356.1, and 356.1–358.0 GHz at a resolution of 0.98 km s$^{-1}$.
The observations with 42 antennas of the 12-m array arranged on baselines between 15 and 1574 m resulted in an angular resolution of about 0.158$''$$\times$0.127$''$ near the line of AlO.
These high angular-resolution observations with a beam of about 34$\times$24 mas are the most detailed observations of Mira to date.
The observations were obtained twice, on 24 Feb. 2014 and 3 May 2014, in nearly the same frequency setup but with different array configurations

findings_qualitative.value: AlO emission is clumpy, absorption seen against the stellar disk, infall of 4–7 km/s suggested

evidence.quote: we imply that the AlO gas captured by the observations is most likely infalling on Mira with a typical velocity of about 4–7 km s$^{-1}$.

claims.hypothesis: Which Al species are observable in Mira?
claims.result: AlO, AlOH, AlH and Al I detected; AlF, AlCl etc. not
claims.finding: AlH, AlO, AlOH, Al I trace gas-phase aluminum

evidence.quote: Our observations show, however, that AlH, AlO, AlOH, and Al I are viable species for tracing gas-phase aluminum in circumstellar envelopes.

claims.result: Flux changes by factor of a few, erratic, uncorrelated with phase

evidence.quote: the pattern of AlO variability in Mira seems very erratic.

claims.result: Average profile shows no depletion beyond 3 R*; one cut shows a deficit
claims.finding: No strong proof for global depletion

evidence.quote: Although there is no strong proof in our data for global AlO depletion, it may be that the gas-phase AlO is consumed by other species only in particular directions.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot trace Al depletion quantitatively; LTE assumption likely violated

evidence.quote: We are unable to quantitatively trace aluminum depletion from the gas
